summary: Design records ownership, retention, metadata, and approval controls. Explore practical exercises and enrol in the course.
lede: Document and records governance training helps records managers and content teams control records across departments. It is designed for records managers, information governance leads, compliance officers and enterprise content managers who need to establish ownership and consistent controls. Participants practise creating records inventories, metadata schemas and retention schedules, and designing quality checks and approval workflows; the course also covers version control, disposition evidence and governance reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who define, operate, or assure document and records controls across departments, repositories, and hybrid teams. Records managers maintaining file plans, retention schedules, and disposition evidence. Information governance leads setting ownership rules and cross-department control standards. Compliance officers checking retention decisions, approval trails, and evidence integrity. Enterprise content managers administering repository structures, metadata, and version controls. Records analysts reconciling inventories and identifying missing or inconsistent metadata. Document control specialists managing controlled versions and review approvals. Information architects mapping document classes to metadata and repository structures. Records operations supervisors coordinating access, retrieval, and disposition work queues. Internal auditors testing records controls and tracing approval evidence. Digital transformation leads designing records requirements for migration and workflow projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with business documents, shared repositories, or records-handling processes is useful. No programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel; access to SharePoint is useful for workflow examples but is not required. Exercises can use anonymized work examples or supplied-in-session scenarios, subject to the delivery setup.
